Clariane announces the success of its €500 million senior notes offering
and the expected signing of its new €700-million revolving credit facility
with terms aligned with the new senior notes
Paris, September 8, 2026
— Clariane (CLARI.PA – ISIN FR0010386334) announces today the success of its offering (the “
Offering
”) of €500 million in aggregate principal amount of new unsecured euro-denominated senior notes due 2032 (the “
Notes
”). The Notes will bear interest at an annual rate of 6.875% and will be issued at a price of 100% of their par value.
The Offering attracted significant interest from a large number of leading institutional investors both in France and abroad, resulting in a solid oversubscription.
The settlement of the Offering is expected to take place on September 21, 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Use of Proceeds

Clariane intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering, together with cash on hand, to (i) repay and cancel in full the term loan facility of €350 million made available under its existing facilities agreement, (ii) repay and cancel in full the real estate term loan facility of €150 million made available under its real estate term loan facility agreement, and (iii) pay fees and expenses in relation to the Offering.

Following the repayment and cancellation of these term loan facilities and the cancellation of the existing revolving credit facility, the existing syndicated facilities agreement, the real estate term loan facility agreement and the related covenants will be terminated.
New €700 million syndicated revolving credit facility with terms aligned with those of the new senior notes

In addition, as announced on September 7, 2026, Clariane has obtained the agreement of its existing and new banking partners subject to the completion of the Offering, to enter into a €700 million unsecured revolving credit facility, which will replace its existing syndicated revolving credit facility. Signing is expected to occur on or around the settlement date of the Offering.

The new revolving credit facility will have a five-year maturity from the signing date and include an accordion feature allowing the facility amount to be increased to up to €900 million. The facility will be able to be used for Clariane’s general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures and the refinancing of the Group’s existing financial indebtedness, excluding hybrid debt.

Drawdowns under the new revolving credit facility will bear interest at a floating rate, corresponding to EURIBOR plus a margin of 1.75% to 3.50%. The applicable margin will be determined on the basis of the total net leverage ratio2 (being the ratio of consolidated net debt of the Group, excluding IFRS 16 liabilities, to consolidated EBITDA of the Group), with an additional ESG-linked margin adjustment mechanism (step-down or step-up events) of up to 6 bps
per annum
, based on performance against three (3) agreed key performance targets3.

The new revolving credit facility will include a semi-annual maintenance covenant requiring the total net leverage ratio of the Group not to exceed 7.00x until June 2027, with a gradual decrease to 6.75x (in December 2027), 6.50x (in June 2028), 6.25x (in December 2028) and 6.00x from June 2029 onwards. No liquidity maintenance covenant will apply under the new revolving credit facility.

The revolving credit facility will also contain customary restrictions on distributions, including a limitation on annual dividend distributions to 7% of Clariane’s market capitalization, subject to consolidated net leverage ratio not exceeding 4.5x.
Guidance confirmed

With respect to its 2023-2026 and 2025-2028 guidance, Clariane confirms all its objectives, it being understood that the terms and conditions applicable under the above-mentioned agreements have no impact on the deleveraging trajectory as set forth in the context of its first-half 2026 results publication,
i.e.
implying a “wholeco” leverage of less than 5.5x at the end of 2026 and of
circa
5.0x by the end of 2028.

This announcement does not constitute and shall not, in any circumstances, constitute a public offering or an invitation to the public in connection with any offer within the meaning of the Prospectus Regulation or otherwise. The offer and sale of the Notes will be made pursuant to an exemption under the Prospectus Regulation from the requirement to produce a prospectus for offers of securities.

In the United Kingdom, this announcement is directed only at (i) persons having professional experience in matters relating to investments falling within Article 19(5) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Financial Promotion) Order 2005 (the “
Order

”), or (ii) high net worth entities falling within Article 49(2)(a) to (d) of the Order, or (iii) persons to whom it would otherwise be lawful to distribute them, all such persons together being referred to as “Relevant Persons.” The Notes are only available to, and any invitation, offer or agreement to subscribe, purchase or otherwise acquire such Notes will be engaged in only with, Relevant Persons.

About Clariane
Clariane is the leading European community for care in times of vulnerability. It has operations in six countries: Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Spain.

Relying on their diverse expertise, each year the Group’s 70,000 professionals provide care and support to more than 840,000 residents and patients in two major areas of activity: Long Term Care and care for frailties, with its networks of medicalized nursing homes and alternative living solutions (Korian, Âges & Vie and Rosorum, etc.), and Specialty Care, which includes medical, post-acute and rehabilitation activities as well as mental health activities (Inicea, Kormed, Iterias, Grupo 5, etc.).
Clariane is a purpose-driven company whose corporate purpose, common to all its activities, is: “taking care of each person’s humanity in times of vulnerability”.
Clariane has been listed on Euronext Paris, Section B since November 2006. The Group joined the SBF 120 index and the CAC® SBT 1.5° index on September 23, 2024.
